rows.name: openDelay?
rows.notes: How long a pointer has to rest on the trigger before the tooltip appears. Long enough that a pointer merely crossing the control never opens one.

rows.name: warmDelay?
rows.notes: The delay once the family is warm — a tooltip is up, or one was up within `warmDuration`. The long delay buys the user protection from tooltips they did not ask for; once they have stopped to read one, they have asked.

rows.name: warmDuration?
rows.notes: How long the family stays warm after the last tooltip closed.

rows.name: closeOnEscape?
rows.notes: Governs the gamepad `back` intent as well: B and Escape share one lock.

rows.name: closeOnScroll?
rows.notes: The anchor is moving out from under the surface; following it is worse.

rows.name: longPress?
rows.notes: Opt-in, and off by default on purpose: a touch device has no hover, so a tooltip there hides its content behind a gesture nothing advertises. Turn it on only where the same information is reachable another way.

rows.name: disabled?
rows.notes: Disables the tooltip, not the trigger.

rows.name: dir?
rows.notes: Not defaulted, deliberately: left unset the resolved page direction governs, so a subtree inside an RTL region inherits instead of being reset to `ltr`.

rows.name: trigger
rows.notes: Handed to `TooltipTrigger` as `render` — never as its children. The trigger *is* a `<button>`, and a button inside a button is `nested-interactive`. Required, unlike `<Dialog trigger>`: see the header — nothing anchors, nothing opens and nothing is described without it.

rows.name: children
rows.notes: The phrase. Required, because a tooltip is only ever this one thing.

rows.name: keepMounted?
rows.notes: Keeps the surface in the markup while closed, `hidden` by state rather than unmounted. Rides in `...root` to `TooltipRoot`, which is where the parts read it from — it is not a machine prop, and the machine never learns about it.
